# Incident Report

MySQL Database Ransomware – corp-pc-a32014

**Analyst:** 	Brian Utley

**Date written:** 	10/6/2026

**Status:** 	Draft for review

# 1\. Executive Summary

On 1 Oct 2026 the Azure-hosted Windows endpoint corp-pc-a32014 (local IP 10.2.0.23) suffered a successful network logon as local Administrator followed by unauthorized MySQL activity. An attacker enumerated and dumped data from the sm\_corp database, dropped multiple databases (including sm\_corp), and left a ransomware note demanding 0.0099 BTC inside a newly created RECOVER\_YOUR\_DATA database. The host continues to receive internet-sourced RDP and authentication attempts. No evidence of file-system encryption was observed in the supplied logs.

# 2\. Incident Details

**Detection window:** First malicious MySQL activity \~19:59–23:05 1 Oct 2026 (MySQL audit); first successful attacker OS logon 22:48 1 Oct 2026\.

**Reporter:** SOC (analysis of Defender Advanced Hunting \+ MySQL audit exports).

**Classification:** Ransomware / Unauthorized Database Access & Destruction – High severity.

**Affected asset:** corp-pc-a32014 (DeviceId ada46642e8721edc3393901e887f744a187af02b), Azure VM running Windows \+ MySQL, exposed RDP (3389) and MySQL.

## KQL DeviceLogonEvents

let MyDevice \= "corp-pc-a32014";

let defaulttime \= datetime(2026-10-02T00:45:15.4042327Z);

DeviceLogonEvents

| where TimeGenerated \>= defaulttime

| where DeviceName \== MyDevice

| where AccountName \=\~ "administrator" and ActionType contains "success"

| project Timestamp, RemoteIP, ActionType, AccountName

*![][image1]*

# 3\. Impact Assessment

**Confidentiality:** SELECT \* FROM sm\_corp.orders executed multiple times – data exfiltration likely.

**Integrity / Availability:** DROP DATABASE sm\_corp, sakila, world (and temporary drop of the ransom DB itself). Business data in sm\_corp is destroyed unless restored from backup.

**Scope:** Single host / single MySQL instance. No lateral movement or additional hosts observed in the provided data.

**Business impact:** Loss of production order data; ransom demand of 0.0099 BTC; continued exposure.

# 6\. Root Cause / Attack Vector

• Host was internet-exposed on RDP (3389) and MySQL.

• Brute-force Network logons against local Administrator succeeded from 200.9.155.148.

• Once on the host (or via direct MySQL access), the attacker obtained/used root@% privileges, dumped sm\_corp.orders, dropped databases, and planted the ransom note.

• Exact initial MySQL authentication vector (weak password, exposed 3306, or post-OS-compromise) is **Not determined from available logs**. No evidence of exploit against JSON\_SCHEMA\_VALID beyond a long-string probe.

# 7\. Response Actions

## Containment

• Immediately block inbound 3389/3306 at NSG / Azure Firewall; restrict to jump-host or VPN only.

• Disable or rename local Administrator; force password reset.

• Quarantine the VM or isolate its NIC.

## Eradication

• Drop any remaining RECOVER\_YOUR\_DATA database and revoke excessive GRANTs on root@%.

• Rotate all MySQL and Windows credentials.

• Review and remove any unauthorized accounts or scheduled tasks (none observed in supplied process/registry data).

## Recovery

• Restore sm\_corp (and any other dropped DBs) from the most recent clean backup taken before 1 Oct 19:59.

• Validate data integrity and re-enable application connectivity only after exposure is closed.

# 8\. Evidence

• DeviceLogonEvents.csv – successful/failed Administrator Network logons.

• mysqlaudit.csv – SELECT on sm\_corp.orders, GRANT statements, CREATE/INSERT of RECOVER\_YOUR\_DATA, DROP DATABASE statements.

• DeviceNetworkEvents.csv – persistent inbound SYN to 3389\.

• DeviceProcessEvents / DeviceFileEvents / DeviceRegistryEvents – no clear OS-level ransomware artifacts observed in the supplied extracts.

• NTANetAnalytics.csv – outbound 80/443 only (no anomalous C2 volumes).

# 9\. Lessons Learned / Recommendations

1. **Immediately** remove public RDP/MySQL exposure; enforce Just-in-Time access or private endpoints.

2. Enforce MFA / disable local Administrator for Network logons; implement account lockout.

3. Enable and alert on MySQL audit events for GRANT, DROP DATABASE, CREATE DATABASE matching “RECOVER\*”.

4. Ensure automated, immutable backups of critical databases with retention that covers the observed dwell time.

5. Hunt historically for the BTC address, onionmail address, and DATAID 23U9Y across all MySQL instances and email gateways.

6. Review Azure NSG / public IP assignments for all VMs running database services.

## **1\. Baseline determination**

I treated PreBreach\_MDE\_Investigation\_Package as the baseline and PostBreachMDE\_Investigation\_Package as the comparison set.

* Baseline collection was at 2026-10-02T02:19:26Z and the post collection at 2026-10-06T21:49:47Z. Both come from the Forensics Collection Summary.csv command timestamps.  
* Boot times agree: SystemInformation.txt shows 10/1 22:44:28 for baseline and 10/6 21:47:50 for post.  
* The Security.evtx records are consistent with that order. Baseline covers 10/1 17:40 to 10/2 02:19. Post covers 10/5 23:40 to 10/6 21:49.  
* Both packages are the same host (Corp-PC-A32014, Windows 11 build 26200, Azure VM, same SIDs).

## **2\. Summary verdict**

Compromise indicators: INCONCLUSIVE, leaning no successful compromise visible. Active attack confirmed. Confidence: moderate.  
The post package holds a large external credential-guessing campaign (28,149 failed network logons) with no successful external logon and no persistence, new services, tasks or accounts in the visible window. But the Security log was flooded so that everything from 10/2 02:19 to 10/5 23:40 was overwritten, so a later success cannot be ruled out.

## **4\. Strongest compromise indicators (ATT\&CK)**

1. Brute force of remote logon (T1110.001/.003, Initial Access / Credential Access).  
   * 62.238.86.212 produced 27,278 of the 28,149 failures. The other sources were 94.26.68.55, 197.13.40.33, 135.125.90.97, 212.11.39.27, 124.158.13.212, 85.211.176.151 and 86.92.53.191.  
   * Usernames tried were ADMINISTRATOR (14,092), USER (4,636), ADMIN (4,635), SERVER (4,563), HP, PC, Administrator and AZUREUSER.  
   * Only 160 attempts reached a password check (status 0xc000006d/0xc000006a), all against administrator. This means the lockout policy stopped almost all of the attack.  
   * There is no 4624 type 3 or 10 from any external IP in the visible window.  
2. Defense impairment by log flooding (T1070, Defense Evasion). The flood pushed 10/2 to 10/5 out of the Security log. I can't tell from the package whether that was intentional or just a side effect of the volume.  
3. Pre-existing weakness (T1078.001/.003). Guest is enabled and in Remote Desktop Users, a decoy-style administrator account exists, and 3389/445/3306/33060 listen on all interfaces. If any of that was unauthorized, it is persistence and privilege abuse by bult's session; a legitimate administrator is more likely, but confirm with them.  
4. Unexplained artifacts (low). The new AUDITPOL.EXE prefetch could indicate someone checking or changing audit policy (T1562.002). The large wct\*.tmp file and the new MMC.EXE prefetch are also unexplained. I found no Event 4719 audit-policy change in post to support the auditpol concern.

## **5\. Probable incident type**

Internet-exposed RDP/SMB credential brute-force or password-spray attempt against a decoy-style administrator account, with no confirmed successful access. Evidence of post-compromise activity (ransomware, exfiltration, persistence) is absent.

## **6\. Gaps**

* Security log: about 3.5 days (10/2 02:19 to 10/5 23:40) are missing, and 10/6 02:29 to 21:47 has no events. A successful logon in that window would be invisible.  
* Other logs: no System, Application or PowerShell logs, and no process-creation audit beyond boot (Event 4688).  
* Missing artifacts: no hosts file, no firewall rule dump (only collector commands in the firewall log), and no browser or credential artifacts. MPSupportFiles.cab in both packages was not unpacked.  
* Not checked: file hashes, signatures and loaded modules (not in these packages), and whether 3389/445 are reachable from the internet (NSG data needed).  
* Prefetch: it cannot be dated or attributed to a user.  
* IOC hunt: the attacker IPs appear 0 times in the baseline and only in post Security.evtx.
